summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, diastolic heart failure, and recurrent E. coli infections was readmitted one day after discharge due to weakness, fever, and dyspnea. She was diagnosed with urosepsis caused by E. coli, confirmed by blood and urine cultures. She also experienced an NSTEMI likely due to sepsis-induced demand ischemia, with elevated troponin and managed with heparin, aspirin, and statin. Her heart failure was managed cautiously due to hypotension; diuresis was initiated once stable. Her transplant medications were adjusted with stress-dose steroids and close monitoring of tacrolimus and sirolimus levels. A PICC line was placed for prolonged IV antibiotic therapy. She improved clinically, with resolution of infection, stabilization of cardiac markers, and recovery of kidney function. She was discharged to extended care for completion of IV ertapenem, with plans for oral fosfomycin prophylaxis, close lab monitoring, and follow-up with cardiology and transplant teams.
